messages.content:
Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Yellow","(B) Blue","(C) Purple","(D) White","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P7972.png"}},"question":"What color is the roof with a special color in the top right corner of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("roof"))
n3=SELECT_SEM($n2,null,"the roof with a special color in the top right corner of the picture",SINGLE,$n1)
n4=ATTRIBUTE($n3,"color")
FINAL($n4,CHOICE_SINGLE)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Orange","(B) Blue","(C) Yellow","(D) Red","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P4320.png"}},"question":"What color are the cranes near the water in the lower right area of this picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("crane"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the cranes near the water in the lower right area",MULTI,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color or colors are visible on the selected object or objects?")

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Blue","(B) Green","(C) Black","(D) Red","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11177.png"}},"question":"What color is the square next to the sports stadium in red at the edge above the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

n1=LOCATE($image0,T("square"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the square next to the sports stadium in red at the edge above the picture",SINGLE,$image0)
n3=ATTRIBUTE($n2,"color")
FINAL($n3,CHOICE_SINGLE)

{"choices":["(A) White","(B) Black","(C) Gray","(D) Orange","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11124.png"}},"question":"What color is the big ship along the left edge of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) White","(B) Orange","(C) Black","(D) Gray","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P11153.png"}},"question":"What color is the house in the upper left area of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_LEFT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("house"))
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color or colors are visible on the selected object or objects?")

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) In the top left corner of the picture.","(B) In the bay on the left edge of the picture.","(C) To the right of the center of the picture.","(D) In the middle bottom of the picture.","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P10169.png"}},"question":"Where is the red cargo ship with a yellow-green circular pattern in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("cargo ship",color="red"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the red cargo ship with a yellow-green circular pattern",SINGLE,$image0)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Black","(B) Pink and White","(C) Blue","(D) Green","(E) This image doesn't feature the color."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P7049.png"}},"question":"What color is the statue on the upper right side of the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=REGION($image0,TOP_RIGHT)
n2=LOCATE($n1,T("statue"))
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"What color or colors are visible on the selected object or objects?")

DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) In the upper left area of the picture","(B) In the upper right area of the picture","(C) In the lower right area of the picture","(D) In the lower left area of the picture","(E) This image doesn't feature the position."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"remote_sensing/dota_v2_dota_v2_dota_v2_P8010.png"}},"question":"Where are the two large planes located in the picture?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OTHER)
n1=LOCATE($image0,T("airplane",size="large"))
n2=SELECT_SEM($n1,null,"the two large planes",MULTI,$image0)
FINAL_QUESTION($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE,"Where in the original image is the selected target or target group?")

COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,

cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and

These chemicals can not only remain as residues in agricultural products but also enter groundwater or nearby water bodies through runoff, leading to water pollution."],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2006/35-2006-0360-6825-LA93.tif"}},"question":"What is the impact of the numerous farmlands shown in the picture on the surrounding environment?","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

FINAL($n1,CHOICE_MULTI)

Compile one remote-sensing question into taskgraph-v1.1-dsl-v1. Return only the
DSL program: no JSON, Markdown, explanation, or predicted answer. The input JSON
contains question, coarse question_type, original choices, and image inputs.
Never copy choices into the program or use a ground-truth answer.

Use only $image0, $image1, ... and sequential n1, n2, ... references. Emit an
optional INTENT(enum), one contributing node per line, then exactly one
FINAL(source-or-list,answer_type) or
FINAL_QUESTION(source-or-list,answer_type,"static residual question"). Final
sources must be $nX references, never raw images.

For a bounding-box localization request, use FINAL($nX,BBOX) with exactly one
single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.

{"choices":["(A) Fields of green crops","(B) The Blue Swimming Pool","(C) The Green Swimming Pool","(D) The Green Lake"],"inputs":{"image0":{"type":"image","uri_or_key":"HRSCD/2006/35-2006-0355-6790-LA93.tif"}},"question":"Identify the object category within the given bounding box in the satellite or aerial image. Image resolution: 10000 x 10000. Bounding box: [3936, 3592, 3952, 3611].","question_type":"MULTIPLE_CHOICE"}

INTENT(OBJECT_CLASSIFICATION)
n1=REGION_BBOX($image0,[3936.0,3592.0,3952.0,3611.0],[10000,10000])
n2=CLASSIFY($n1)
FINAL($n2,CHOICE_SINGLE)

single-target visual source and omit a residual final question. Prefer the
shortest faithful path: LOCATE for category/intrinsic attributes, REGION then
LOCATE for an explicit image area, or a singleton SELECT for an extreme,
ordinal, or external semantic condition. BBOX is not a choice answer. Its
source must be LOCATE, REGION/REGION_BBOX, or SELECT_RANK/ORD/EXTREME/SUBREGION
or SELECT_SEM(...,SINGLE). Do not pass GROUP, SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM MULTI, or
multiple sources directly to BBOX. Runtime must reject zero/multiple targets
and unresolved evidence; never predict bbox coordinate values in the program.

Allowed node surfaces are REGION, REGION_BBOX, FIND_MARKER, LOCATE with T(...),
SELECT_REL, SELECT_SEM, SELECT_RANK, SELECT_ORD, SELECT_EXTREME, SELECT_SUBREGION, GROUP,
COUNT, COUNT_IMAGE, COUNT_ENTITIES, ATTRIBUTE, CLASSIFY, MULTILABEL_CLASSIFY,
MOTION, RELATION, ABS_DIFF, VLM_REASON, BUILD_ROUTE_CONTEXT, and ROUTE_REASON.
Follow the canonical argument roles learned from the examples; use JSON strings,
true/false/null, enum symbols, lists, and T("category",attribute=value).

Prefer dedicated deterministic operators over VLM_REASON. COUNT is mandatory
and authoritative for counting. Relational counting must filter with SELECT and
feed that result to COUNT_ENTITIES or COUNT_IMAGE. Preserve explicit category
alternatives, attributes, positions, markers, bounding boxes, relations, ranks,
ordinals, groups, and route endpoints. SELECT_RANK criterion must be exactly
the quoted string "bbox_area" or "score": rank by the bounding-box area
(largest/smallest object) or by detector score only. Use FINAL_QUESTION only
when visual or semantic evidence still needs a final judgment; never include
runtime values. When a complex
question needs both a COUNT result and visual evidence, keep COUNT upstream and feed the mixed
evidence into one VLM_REASON node; use only that node as the final source.

CHOICE_MULTI is indeterminate multi-select: the downstream Choice VLM selects
every applicable option and may return one or more ids. CHOICE_SINGLE permits
exactly one id. Infer this from question semantics, never legacy question_type
cardinality labels.

For a natural-language condition over existing candidates, use
SELECT_SEM(candidates,reference-or-null,"complete natural language query",SINGLE|MULTI[,scope]).
The optional fifth argument is an ImageRef or preceding Region reference and
maps only to SELECT.inputs.scope. Omit it when no explicit scope is needed;
do not insert a default or null. Scope and reference are separate input roles.
The string belongs to SELECT.params.query, never to inputs. Preserve the full
condition (including surrounding trees, grass, roads, shapes, and spatial context).
Do not create extra LOCATE nodes for background nouns solely to express this
condition. LOCATE produces the category candidates with their intrinsic TargetSpec
attributes; SELECT consumes the filtering condition. SINGLE may be ambiguous or
unresolved; MULTI may select no candidates. Geometry REL/RANK/ORD/EXTREME and
SUBREGION remain available and retain their meanings. Plan all logical steps
explicitly; the executor chooses only physical LOCATE backends from their uses.
